blocks: There is no port to talk to. The PM3 12V series is a switch-mode AC/DC converter/charger whose entire external interface, per the manufacturer's own manual, is: a captive 120 VAC line cord, a chassis bonding lug, + and - 12 VDC output terminals, two reversed-battery fuses, one LED status light, a temperature-controlled fan, and two internal adjusters (switch A = three-stage vs. fixed-voltage, switch B = output trim 13-16.5 V). No RS-485, no RS-232, no CAN, no Bluetooth, no WiFi, no remote-panel jack, no dry contact, no battery temperature sense lead. No driver is possible and none should be planned. The only way this unit becomes observable is indirectly, from a metered AC source upstream (a smart plug on the AC feed) or a DC shunt downstream - which is exactly the arrangement already recorded for the PM4-55LK installed at this site in docs/catalog/no-comms.md.

The retail sighting and PowerMax's own PM3 12V product page both list an 85 A option, but neither vendor document names one: the owner's manual enumerates 15/35/45/55/60/65/75/100/120 and the Nov-2023 spec sheet tabulates only 35/45/55/60/65/75/100. Coverage is wider than the retail sighting. The vendor documents also cover PM3-60, PM3-65 and PM3-120, and 220 VAC variants (PM3-55E/75E/100E) have a separate spec sheet. All the same no-comms entry; the catalogue does not need a second pass for them.

PM3-15 is in the owner's manual and on the product page but absent from the Nov-2023 spec sheet table. Likely dropped from the current line rather than a documentation error, but the vendor does not say.
Retail SKUs carry an LK suffix (PM3-55LK) that the manual drops (PM3-55). The spec sheet uses LK throughout. Same unit; the suffix is not a comms variant.

Do not infer comms from other PowerMax products. PowerMax does sell Bluetooth-capable gear - the PCW wireless RV power centres, the PMDP-30/50-BT distribution panel, and their LiFePO4 smart batteries - and the PM3-SME carries an on-unit meter.
